title: South Korean wallet maker DCENT to end App Wallet service after September crypto thefts
date_note: Date of the Yonhap report as cited by Crypto.news; the pages give no earlier day for the shutdown decision.
geo_basis: company is South Korean, as the sources state; city not stated
summary: Crypto.news and Coin Edition report that DCENT is ending its App Wallet service, which they say affects software wallets and not hardware devices. Customers reported suspicious transactions on 16 September. Coin Edition says 12.728 million XRP was valued at roughly 15.4 billion won; neither page names a confirmed cause. DCENT's 2 November notice says the issue does not affect the hardware wallet devices.
plain: DCENT is ending its app-based wallet after customers reported suspicious crypto transfers in September. The company says its hardware wallets are not affected. No cause has been confirmed.
exec: A Korean wallet maker is closing its app wallet after reported thefts; no cause is confirmed, and the company says hardware wallets are unaffected.
action: DCENT advises users who entered the same recovery phrase into the App Wallet to create a new wallet with a new recovery phrase and move their remaining assets.

evidence.quote: The 12.728 million XRP was valued at roughly 15.4 billion won.

validation.note: Crypto.news and Coin Edition both report the App Wallet shutdown and the September transactions, each relaying Yonhap. DCENT's own notice was not read; its statement is as quoted by Crypto.news.
